subject: Azura Pay — performance goals & streaming preferences
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <pri.r@azurapay.com>, Azura Pay Engineering <eng@azurapay.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap & ask: performance targets, TTFT, and streaming approach

Hi Priya / Azura team,

Thanks for the productive call earlier — listing the items we agreed on and a couple of clarifying questions so we can scope the pilot and SLO doc.

Summary of what I heard (please correct if I missed anything):
- Primary UX: in-product payments flow (interactive) with live validation and risk-checks.
- Target TTFT (time-to-first-token): goal of ~150ms typical, allow up to 250ms P95 for interactive flows.
- Throughput & concurrency: peak concurrent requests ~250, average steady-state ~60–80 rps.
- Streaming: you need incremental tokens to start rendering UI; prefer WebSocket because of your browser proxying, but open to SSE if simpler.
- Chunk cadence preference: client prefers small frequent chunks for smooth UX — approx 100–200ms cadence or ~64–128 token chunks.
- Data/PII: no raw card numbers in prompts; we’ll treat payloads as sensitive.

Next technical asks from our side to make a pilot proposal:
1) Can you share a representative 1–2 day traffic sample (anonymized) and an example prompt -> desired rendering behavior?
2) Confirm which browser proxies (WAF/NGINX) will terminate WebSocket connections — we’ll need to mirror that in our staging network.
3) For TTFT, please confirm whether you want P50 or P95 as the billing/alerting anchor (our SLOs can track both).

I attached a short SLO proposal (slo-proposal-azura.pdf) and a CSV template for traffic (azurapay_mvp_traffic.csv). If the targets above look right, I’ll put together a two-week pilot plan with specific perf gates and a proposed runbook.

Proposed immediate next step: send us the traffic sample and confirm WebSocket vs SSE preference by EOD Monday 05/31.

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Quick recap & ask: performance targets, TTFT, and streaming approach

Thanks Rachel — quick answers inline and attaching the anonymized export.

On Thu, May 28, 2026 at 3:02 PM Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Target TTFT (time-to-first-token): goal of ~150ms typical, allow up to 250ms P95 for interactive flows.

To clarify: 150ms is the UX target we want to shoot for in ideal networks — for alerts and SLOs we care about P95. Our acceptable SLO floor is 250ms P95 for interactive endpoints; backend batch validation endpoints can be looser (up to 400ms P95).

> - Throughput & concurrency: peak concurrent requests ~250, average steady-state ~60–80 rps.

Confirmed. Peak concurrency hits during heavy settlement windows (UTC 01:00–02:00) — see attached sample.

> - Streaming: you need incremental tokens to start rendering UI; prefer WebSocket because of your browser proxying, but open to SSE if simpler.

We prefer WebSocket since our frontend stack already upgrades connections and we have sticky routing; SSE is acceptable only if WebSocket is blocked by client environments.

> - Chunk cadence preference: client prefers small frequent chunks for smooth UX — approx 100–200ms cadence or ~64–128 token chunks.

That cadence aligns with our UX team guidance. If you recommend an alternative that gives stronger TTFT guarantees, happy to discuss.

Attached: azurapay_mvp_traffic.csv (anonymized 48h sample).

Next: I propose a technical kickoff next Wed 06/02 — can your SE join? Also share the pilot runbook draft once you have it.

Best,
Priya
Head of Platform, Azura Pay
pri.r@azurapay.com

Attachments: azurapay_mvp_traffic.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <pri.r@azurapay.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap & ask: performance targets, TTFT, and streaming approach

Thanks Priya — got the sample. I pulled a quick profile and here are proposed technical recommendations for the pilot (high level):

Key perf anchors we’ll validate in the pilot:
- TTFT: aim for median ~120ms, P95 <= 220–250ms for interactive endpoint under representative network conditions. We’ll report both P50/P95.
- Chunk cadence: target 120–180ms per chunk, sizing ~64 tokens as default; we’ll tune to 32–128 token range depending on generation distribution.
- Concurrency: validate up to 300 concurrent streams with graceful degradation and fallbacks to smaller model/quantized variant.
- Throughput: pilot traffic size suggestion = 2M tokens/day, with burst window testing up to 3x traffic for autoscaling validation.

Technical levers we recommend:
- Use continuous batching with per-client affinity to reduce cold-prefix latency.
- Enable KV cache for repeated prompt prefixes (payment templates).
- Run with int8 quantization candidate in staging to reduce per-token latency/cost; fall back to fp16 for quality comparisons.
- WebSocket recommended: our runtime supports both SSE and WS; WS will avoid some proxy-induced buffering. We’ll provide a small JS example for your frontend.

Pilot plan (two-week):
- Week 0 (prep): set up staging endpoints, share test credentials, run synthetic baseline.
- Week 1 (controlled): replay your 48h sample at 0.5–1.0x to validate correctness & perf.
- Week 2 (ramp): 1–2x real traffic plus burst tests; finalize SLO thresholds and rollback rules.

Open items before kickoff:
1) Confirm WebSocket (you indicated yes) and provide proxy/WAF behavior details by Mon 05/31.
2) Grant our staging account IP range access to your preprod CORS/WAF for end-to-end testing.
3) Confirm a 60–90 minute technical kickoff slot on Wed 06/02 (we propose 10:00–11:30 PT).

I attached a short runbook template and will post the JS WebSocket example to the Doc linked in the thread.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher

sean.gallagher@redwood.com

Confirmed items:

- WebSocket as primary streaming transport; Redwood will provide a short JS snippet and config recommendations for sticky routing.
- Chunk cadence: initial default 120ms cadence / ~64-token chunks; SE will tune after week 1 replays.

Action checklist (owners & target dates):

- Azura: confirm IP/CIDR allowlist for Redwood staging (owner: Priya) — due Mon 05/31.
- Redwood (Sean): post WS example + runbook draft to the Doc and share link — due Mon 05/31.
- Redwood (Rachel): create pilot runbook in HubSpot & send invite for Wed 06/02 10:00–11:30 PT technical kickoff — scheduled.

If all of the above looks right I’ll mark the HubSpot deal AZP-4721 as "pilot_planned" and circulate the kickoff invite.

Onward — looking forward to getting this running.
